primary_conclusion: Endpoint direction is valid but discards bps magnitude. The fixed terminal readout now improves TRAIN fitting substantially without supported later AUC5 improvement and with worse later proper scores. Simple final-head underfit is therefore weakened as the sole actionable explanation on fold1. Stable forward signal, upstream representation learning and target mismatch remain unresolved; no sign bug or economic edge established.

findings.classification: Prefix head underfit is measured; a simple final-head refit is not supported as a later-direction remedy on the tested fold. Backbone exposure and representation learning remain plausible, not isolated errors.
findings.mechanism: The fixed nonlinear ET252 comparator ranks five-minute outcomes better than the native three-logit decoder after checked equal local input values. The gap may arise from head fitting, shared representation learning or insufficient exposure.
findings.counterevidence: Representations, normalization fit populations, history and learners differ. The result is reused development evidence, not independent or economic edge. One pass does not demonstrate convergence. The tested fold1ET252AUC5 is .50134359, below native .50302109: the earlier fourfold ET advantage cannot be assigned to this one fold.
findings.smallest_decisive_test: Completed: full47602prefix/17288later terminal-only frozen-linear readout, same original head and masks, three fixed converged fits and paired4000day/week replicates. Do not rerun it or relabel the outcome as an optimization failure.
findings.expected_if_true: Better later ranking with the same frozen hidden localizes a correctable decoder/optimization contribution.
findings.weakens_if: A numerically qualified, adequately fitted linear readout does not improve later ranking; this weakens simple head underfit but does not prove all predictive information absent.
findings.minimum_improvement: Do not replace the native head with this fitted candidate. Further exposure is a separate unchanged-target one-versus-three-pass hypothesis and requires fresh bounded design; no30-epoch escalation.
findings.stop: Require complete cohorts, exact representation/label identity and qualified solver convergence. Stop on guard or identity failure; no repeat hyperparameter or threshold search.
findings.actual_outcome: The prespecified weakening outcome occurred: all3TRAINAUC/proper scores improved, no supported laterAUC5gain, laterproperworse3/3. This is one reused fold, not proof that all backbone optimization or more epochs cannot help.

findings.classification: Proven source-level supervision limitation, not a sign bug or demonstrated explanation for weak endpoint AUC.
findings.mechanism: The projector computes signed mid_return_bps, but the training adapter selects terminal_time_ns, observed and sign. Equal logits receive equal BCE and gradients for +0.1 and +50bps. Observed zero returns are excluded from BCE.

measured_support.evidence_class: source/algebra only; no new market measurement

findings.counterevidence: Sign-only BCE is appropriate for probability of a positive nonzero endpoint. Adding magnitude may add noise and cannot be presumed to fix directional ranking. The fact that +0.1 and +50bps share a target does not show that small moves dominate this dataset; that empirical distribution has not yet been measured in this analysis.
findings.smallest_decisive_test: First measure the unmeasured premise using existing saved TRAIN targets/predictions: exactjoin per horizon, full magnitude/missing/zero distribution and contribution of fixed absolute-bps bands to eligible-cell loss. Report every predeclared band; conditioning on realized magnitude is diagnostic and is not an executable filter. Then compare one magnitude component at unchanged horizons/exposure if the mechanism is supported.
findings.expected_if_true: Improved later magnitude/distribution proper scores with preserved or improved direction, not merely TRAIN fit.
findings.weakens_if: Later magnitude or direction does not improve, or any gain disappears when training exposure is matched.
findings.minimum_improvement: Add only the measured useful magnitude component. Do not relabel inactive legacy path heads as current supervision.
findings.stop: No arbitrary weighting after results, no target-dependent filtering to select big winning moves, no simultaneous horizon/epoch/input change.

findings.classification: Proven algebraic consequence of the current loss reduction; dense-horizon benefit remains unmeasured.
findings.mechanism: The current loss divides the sum of eligible BCE cells by their count. With complete masks each old horizon has one third of weight. A naive 60-horizon extension gives each one sixtieth and places45of60cells after15minutes. Shared hidden couples gradients, but there is no explicit return-size or joint path loss.

measured_support.evidence_class: source/algebra; no60-output model exists in this comparison

findings.counterevidence: Dense endpoints can capture excursions missed between sparse endpoints. Longer-horizon emphasis may be a legitimate choice if declared;60marginal probabilities still do not determine a joint price path or intraminute order. This potential60-horizon weighting problem cannot explain the currently observed1/5/15results: no60-horizon native model has been trained.
findings.smallest_decisive_test: First qualify exact D+h targets, per-horizon masks and legacy1/5/15parity on synthetic clocks. Then, only under fresh admission, compare one declared horizon extension at fixed exposure and predeclared horizon weighting. Report all six anchors and one fixed curve score.
findings.expected_if_true: The declared extension improves later curve/anchor scores without masking deterioration at original horizons.
findings.weakens_if: Only posthoc selected minutes improve, or the apparent gain follows changed eligibility or changed relative horizon weight.
findings.minimum_improvement: Use an explicit horizon contract and weights; do not merely change a constant from3to60. Preserve the original baseline and M5 decision cadence.
findings.stop: Stop on timestamp, source-row, maturity, zero/missing, shape or baseline parity failure. Do not interpolate missing labels or automatically extend epochs.

findings.classification: Plausible explanation; predictive information loss has not been demonstrated.
findings.mechanism: GC and base projections are added, sequence representations use mean plus last, family/timeframe tokens are weighted and pooled, and concatenated representations pass through LayerNorm,512-to128projection and GELU.

measured_support.evidence_limit: Variance change does not quantify retained predictive information.

findings.counterevidence: Low variance can preserve ranking; asinh has no hard continuous clip and is invertible before finite precision. Temporal positions, latest-bar state, M5 and higher-timeframe identities already exist. Gate weights and parameter changes are not utility evidence.
findings.smallest_decisive_test: Now that the qualified final-hidden readout failed the primary later criterion, a separately justified earlier-representation comparison may test lost accessible signal. Keep identical prefix/later rows and learner; explicitly control width, scaling and fitting capacity, since simply moving from128to512features confounds representation with decoder capacity.
findings.expected_if_true: Earlier representation predicts later outcomes better under the same fitted learner while final-hidden fitting is adequate.
findings.weakens_if: Final-hidden readout recovers the ranking, or earlier representation has no controlled advantage.
findings.minimum_improvement: One narrow connection preserving the specific earlier information shown useful; retain all eight families and D1/macro.
findings.stop: No broad architecture or indicator search; no family removal from a weak small test.

findings.classification: Prediction rule proven by source; partial probability-level defect measured; raw-feature drivers and market causation unmeasured.
findings.mechanism: For each horizon z=b+w^T hidden, UP iff z>0, otherwise DOWN. A shift in bias can make all hard decisions UP while logits still rank outcomes. This does not identify which raw input drives each decision, and the research head does not issue trades.

measured_support.interpretation: Fixed TRAIN-only offsets improved the predeclared5mproper-score criterion without improving ranking; bias alone cannot explain the ET252 ranking deficit.

findings.counterevidence: AUC and hard decisions answer different questions. Recalibration cannot repair rank. Attention or gate weights are not causal attributions to price movement.
findings.smallest_decisive_test: For a separately admitted fixed set of predictions, decompose the exact bias and w^T hidden before investigating one justified raw-family sensitivity with coherent masks and derived relations. Distinguish model sensitivity from predictive value and real-world causation.
findings.expected_if_true: The decomposition explains hard direction changes; any proposed feature improvement must subsequently improve predefined later prediction scores.
findings.weakens_if: Bias does not dominate the chosen decision changes; raw-feature interventions fail coherence or do not improve later prediction.
findings.minimum_improvement: Retain explicit probability, uncertainty and decision threshold in reporting. Do not make further threshold tuning the primary edge investigation.
findings.stop: No posthoc winning thresholds or subgroups; no market-causal claims from model sensitivities.

preferred_target_definition.joint_path_warning: Minute-specific probabilities and marginal quantiles describe endpoints, not the probability of an entire rise-and-reversal trajectory. A claim about first movement, first favorable excursion or a turn requires explicit path/order supervision.
